questions.stem: An oil record book is used to:
options: List the spare parts kept on board
Log the engine running hours only
Record the crew's certificates
Record oil transfers, bunkering and bilge discharges
questions.explanation: An oil record book documents the vessel's handling of oil and oily mixtures where regulations require one: transfers, bunkering and bilge discharges. It is not a parts list, crew record or running-hours log.

questions.stem: One essential thing to have in place before bunkering starts is:
options: Reliable communication with the fuel source
The engine-room temperature reading
The tide height at the fuel dock
A full crew list signed by the master and the supplier
questions.explanation: Reliable communication between the vessel and the fuel source means the transfer can be stopped at once if something goes wrong. The engine-room temperature, the tide and the menu do not affect the safety of the transfer.

questions.stem: A Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) is mainly used:
options: To plan routine engine maintenance
To order spare parts and stores
As a record of fuel consumption
As a guide for responding to an oil spill
questions.explanation: It lists who to call and what to do to stop and contain a spill.

questions.stem: If your vessel causes or may have caused pollution you should:
options: Wait until the next port and report it there
Record it only in the engine log
Report it immediately to the Coast Guard
Disperse it with detergent first
questions.explanation: Report promptly to the Coast Guard through MCTS, then follow your emergency plan.

questions.stem: The bilge contains a film of oil. The most appropriate action is to:
options: Pump it to a holding tank or drums for disposal ashore
Leave it and wait for it to evaporate in the warm weather
Add detergent and then pump it out with the bilge
Pump it overboard once you are well clear of land
questions.explanation: Oily bilge water is kept on board and landed at a reception facility. Detergent only hides the oil and spreads the harm.

questions.stem: Which is a typical source of oil pollution from a small vessel's engine room?
options: Grey water from a shower drain
Overflow from a tank vent during bunkering
Clean cooling water from the exhaust outlet
Air from the compressor unloader
questions.explanation: Overfilled tanks, leaks, bilge water and sludge are the common sources. Properly cooled exhaust water is not oil pollution.

Watch the level, stay at the valves, stop well short of full
Leave the connection while you do other jobs
Rely only on the gauge to tell you when to stop
questions.explanation: Most spills happen at the fuel dock. Stay in control, sound the tank, and leave space for expansion.

questions.stem: Before bunkering you should plug the scuppers and put out drip trays because:
options: They stop the tank from filling too fast
A small spill is caught on deck, not in the water
They keep the deck tidy for the inspector
They keep the fuel warm as it is being transferred
questions.explanation: Drip trays and plugged scuppers contain small spills. A spill kept on the deck is a clean-up, but one that reaches the water is a reportable incident.

questions.stem: Why should detergent not be used on a small oil spill on the water?
options: It is too expensive to carry on board
It makes the oil sink out of sight and is always allowed
It turns the oil back into usable fuel
It spreads the oil, may do more harm, and needs approval
questions.explanation: Dispersants and detergents are controlled. Contain the spill with sorbents and report it, and use chemicals only if the authorities approve.

questions.stem: Which statement about plastic garbage is correct?
options: It may be thrown overboard beyond 3 nautical miles
Plastic must never be thrown overboard
It may be thrown overboard if cut up
It may be burned on deck
questions.explanation: Plastics persist and kill wildlife. Keep them on board and dispose of them ashore.
